Part 1: The 30-Second Elevator Pitch (What to Say First)
Verbatim Speech Script for Professor / Evaluator:
"Sir, my project is titled 'SIMD Vectorization of Color Appearance Models (CAM16) for Efficient Computation' in Computer Organization and Architecture. In modern 4K/8K video processing, HDR displays, and color grading, the international CIE CAM16 standard must process millions of pixels per second. However, standard implementations in Python or C++ take seconds because CAM16 relies on non-linear fractional powers (x0.42), transcendental arctangent functions (atan2), and piecewise quadrant branches.

I engineered an explicit 256-bit AVX2 SIMD C++ engine from scratch using <immintrin.h>. Tested on bare-metal AMD Ryzen 7 7435HS hardware, our manual AVX2 engine achieves 47.28 Million colors per second—delivering a 12.32× speedup over the scalar baseline and 8.61× over compiler auto-vectorization, while remaining strictly perceptually lossless (ΔE << 1.0)."
Part 2: Why This is a Real COA Problem (3 Microarchitectural Bottlenecks)
  • Memory Alignment & Layout Bottleneck (AoS vs. SoA): Standard graphics libraries store pixels in Array-of-Structures ([X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1, ...]). Fetching eight X values requires strided loads, wasting 66% of fetched cache lines. We restructured data into 32-byte aligned Structure-of-Arrays (SoA: X[], Y[], Z[]), enabling single-cycle 256-bit vector loads (_mm256_load_ps) with 100% cache-line utilization.
  • Transcendental Function & ABI Bottleneck: CAM16 relies on std::powf(x, 0.42) and std::atan2f(b, a). Standard compilers cannot auto-vectorize loops calling libm due to C calling conventions, stack frame overhead, and errno preservation. These functions account for ≈70% of total runtime.
  • Pipeline Branch Misprediction Bottleneck: Computing Hue Quadrature (H) requires 4-quadrant piecewise if-else checks. In superscalar CPUs, dynamic branching causes mispredictions, flushing the 14–19 stage execution pipeline.

Part 4: The 5 Microarchitectural Innovations Engineered in C++
  • In-Register Cody-Waite Range Reduction & Minimax Exponentiation (x0.42, t0.9): Replaced scalar powf() with bit-level IEEE 754 exponent extraction (_mm256_srli_epi32) and a 9th-degree Chebyshev/Minimax polynomial evaluated strictly through chained Fused Multiply-Add instructions (_mm256_fmadd_ps). Reduces power latency from ≈120 cycles to 14 cycles.
  • Vector Rational Arctangent (avx2_atan2_deg): Replaced scalar atan2f() with Abramowitz & Stegun Formula 4.4.49 10th-degree rational minimax approximation inside 256-bit YMM registers. Computes 8 angle lanes in parallel with error < 0.0002°.
  • Algebraic Trigonometric Elimination: Eliminated expensive runtime trigonometric calls in eccentricity et = 0.25[cos(h + 2) + 3.8] via the identity cos(h + 2) = [a·cos(2) - b·sin(2)] / √(a2 + b2). Evaluated using fast reciprocal square root (_mm256_rsqrt_ps) and two FMAs.
  • Branchless Vector Masking (_mm256_blendv_ps): Replaced 4-quadrant piecewise if-else branches in Hue Quadrature (H) with vector comparison masks (_mm256_cmp_ps) and conditional blending. Eliminates branch mispredictions completely, locking latency to a deterministic 18 cycles.
  • Dual 256-bit FMA Pipeline Saturation: AMD Zen 3+/4 cores contain two independent 256-bit FMA execution ports. We structured independent instruction streams so the superscalar out-of-order scheduler issues two 256-bit vector operations per clock cycle.

COA Architectural Insight: High Arithmetic Intensity
Notice throughput drops by only 4.0% between L1/L2 cache (47.28 Mcps) and main DDR5 DRAM (45.38 Mcps). This occurs because CAM16 executes ≈130 floating-point operations while loading only 12 bytes per pixel (≈10.8–12.8 FLOPs/byte). The engine is strictly compute/FMA-bound rather than memory bandwidth-bound.

Top 6 Professor Questions
Part 8: Top Viva Voce / Professor Questions & Architectural Defense
Q1 Why did GCC Auto-Vectorization (-O3) achieve only 1.43× speedup?
Answer: Governed by Amdahl's Law. GCC auto-vectorizes Stage 1 linear matrix math into 8-wide FMAs, but cannot vectorize Stages 2–5 because std::powf() and std::atan2f() are external libm calls. The compiler must adhere to the C ABI calling convention and preserve errno. Because non-linear math takes ≈70% of execution time, Amdahl's Law limits auto-vec speedup to 1 / [(1-0.70)/8 + 0.70] ≈ 1.36×, matching our empirical 1.43×.
Q2 How did you evaluate fractional powers (x0.42, t0.9) in AVX2?
Answer: Using Cody-Waite range reduction and a 9th-degree Minimax polynomial: we split float x into 2n · m (m ∈ [0.707, 1.414]) using integer shift intrinsics (_mm256_srli_epi32). We evaluate log2(m) with a polynomial, multiply by 0.42, and evaluate 2y via polynomial FMA instructions (_mm256_fmadd_ps). This eliminates libm calls, executing in 14 cycles instead of 120 cycles.
Q3 How did you eliminate branch mispredictions in Hue Quadrature (H)?
Answer: Using branchless vector masking. Instead of scalar if-else branches for the 4 quadrants, we evaluate comparisons using _mm256_cmp_ps, producing 256-bit bitmasks (all 1s or all 0s). We then blend the correct quadrant constants using _mm256_blendv_ps. This eliminates branch prediction stalls and locks latency to a fixed 18 cycles.
Q4 Did your polynomial approximations degrade perceptual accuracy?
Answer: No. In color science, ΔE ≈ 1.0 defines one Just Noticeable Difference (JND). Across 10,000 test colors against Python 64-bit double precision, maximum Lightness error is 0.000359—which is 2,785× smaller than 1 JND. Maximum relative error across all correlates is < 0.002%, guaranteeing the output is strictly perceptually lossless.
Q5 Why did performance barely drop between L1 cache and main DRAM?
Answer: Because of CAM16's high Arithmetic Intensity (≈12.8 FLOPs per byte loaded). The CPU performs ≈130 operations per 12-byte sample. This high operational density keeps the execution units fully saturated, making the pipeline compute-bound rather than memory-bandwidth bound.
Q6 Why 32-bit single-precision floats instead of 64-bit doubles?
Answer: In 256-bit AVX2, we pack 8 single-precision floats versus only 4 doubles, doubling raw throughput. Because single-precision error is 2,785× below the human perception limit, double precision provides zero visual benefit while halving compute throughput.
